summary.text: 样 means “form” or “shape” and is the standardized simplified counterpart of 樣. The traditional graph is analyzed with 木 for a tree or wood category and 羕 as its sound element. Simplified 样 has 羊 in that position; the reason is undocumented.

formation.text: Traditional 樣 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 木 contributes a tree or wood category, and 羕 supplies a sound cue. A historical dictionary glosses it as an oak fruit, but that does not establish the earliest meaning or a path to later senses. The 1956 scheme standardizes 样 as the simplified counterpart of 樣 without explaining the change from 羕 to 羊.

components.text: In traditional 樣, 木 contributes the tree or wood category. A historical dictionary account connects it with an oak-fruit gloss.

In traditional 樣, 羕 is identified as the phonetic element. The curated seal-style drawing is a modern redraw of a traditional lexicographic form, not a dated specimen of 樣. Simplified 样 has 羊 in this position; the reason for the change is undocumented.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Old Chinese comparison supports a sound relationship but does not independently establish the component’s identity or role. Current readings do not prove an ancient sound relation.

sound.text: Zhengzhang-style Old Chinese reconstructs both 羕 and 樣 as *laŋs, supporting the proposed phonetic relation in this system.
The supplied local Mandarin readings match: 羕 is yàng and the scoped host 樣 is yàng. This modern match alone does not establish their historical sound relation.

history.text: The 1956 simplification scheme lists 样（樣） as standardized simplified and traditional counterparts. It does not explain why 羕 became 羊 within the simplified graph.

The curated image is a modern seal-style redraw of 羕 in a traditional lexicographic style. It is not a dated artifact or a sequence of forms for 樣; the character’s earliest attestation and dated graphic history remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: A historical dictionary account gives 樣 the referent “oak fruit,” but this is not established as its earliest meaning. The evidence does not show how, or whether, that sense developed into later senses such as form, shape, kind, sample, or classifier.

The distinct older graph 样 is recorded with the reading yáng for a wooden support post for silkworm trays, and with yàng as a variant referring to 樣. Its date and relationship to the standardized simplified form are not fully explained.

No independent evidence supports borrowing a tree or oak name to write “form” or “pattern” because of similar sound. The traditional analysis identifies 羕 as 樣’s sound element but does not establish that separate borrowing mechanism.

A cited Song poem uses 樣 for kind or type. This establishes an example by the Song period, not when the sense originated or its chronology relative to other senses.

evidence.text: The dictionary account associates 樣 with 木 and 羕, and glosses the old referent as an oak fruit (櫟實); this supports a tree-related semantic component and 羕 as phonetic in the traditional graph. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the earliest form.

evidence.source: Chinese Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.text: Lists 樣 yàng for form/shape, kind, a standard sample, and a classifier. It cites Du Fu’s Tang poem 楊監又出畫鷹十二扇, with 樣 meaning a model/form, and a Song poem by Yang Wanli for the ‘kind’ sense. It separately records xiàng as equivalent to 橡. These are separate senses; the listings do not establish a chronology among them.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》: 樣

evidence.source: Chinese Character Simplification Scheme, State Council resolution reproduced by Wikisource
evidence.text: The resolution is dated 1956-01-28 and states that first-table simplified characters were to be used from 1956-02-01. The table explicitly gives 样（樣）. This supports 樣 → 样 as a standardized simplified counterpart. The document does not explain the historical origin of 樣’s 羕 component.
evidence.title: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议 / 汉字简化方案

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry, citing Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003)
evidence.text: Lists 樣 in a 羊-related phonetic series, with Zhengzhang-style Old Chinese *laŋs for 樣 and *laŋ for 羊, and describes the traditional graph as 木 semantic plus 羕 phonetic. This is one reconstruction system and a secondary summary; it supports a historical sound relationship but does not by itself date the graph or establish the original referent of 羕.
evidence.title: 樣 - 維基詞典

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese entry, citing Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003)

evidence.field: 說文釋形; 注音; 釋義
evidence.text: The distinct graph 样 is not included in Shuowen; the dictionary gives it readings yáng and yàng. Its yáng sense is a wooden pillar used to support trays for raising silkworms, attributed to Guangyun; the yàng sense is referred to 樣 as a variant. This distinction cautions against treating every occurrence of 样 as the simplified form of 樣.
evidence.title: 样 - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.field: headword; meanings and cited literary usage
evidence.text: The entry separates yàng from xiàng (the latter referred to 橡). For yàng it lists form/shape and cites Du Fu’s Tang poem 楊監又出畫鷹十二扇, with 樣 in 能畫鷙鳥樣; it lists kind and cites Yang Wanli’s Song poem 曉出淨慈送林子方, with 別樣紅. It also records sample/model and a classifier, giving 六樣小菜. This verifies the classifier as a recorded use and provides dated literary examples for form/shape and kind; the examples do not establish when those senses originated or their semantic order.

evidence.text: Reports the Shuowen definition 栩實 and analysis 从木，羕聲, with fanqie 徐兩切. It describes the modern traditional form’s right component as 羕, with 羊 written in its upper-side form and 永 below. The entry lists form/shape, kind, model/sample, classifier and the separate xiàng reading equivalent to 橡. It indexes Shuowen, Ganlu zishu, Yupian, Jiyun and other witnesses, but the page does not provide an artifact-dated sequence of 樣 forms.

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, Four-Part Series edition, reproduced by Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷第六上, 木部 entry
evidence.text: The inspected text identifies its basis as a Northern Song printed edition held in the Iwasaki/Sekidō collection. In the 木 section it gives 樣 as 栩實，從木羕聲，徐兩切. This is a direct textual witness to the historical dictionary’s oak-fruit gloss and 木-plus-羕 analysis, not an excavated early inscription or proof that oak fruit was the earliest use.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: Reports 羕 as 水長也, analyzed as 从𣱵，羊聲, fanqie 余亮切, and gives modern Mandarin yàng. Thus 羕 itself contains 羊 as a sound element, while 樣’s traditional compound uses the whole graph 羕 as its phonetic component. The dictionary entry does not establish the full historical phonetic development.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The earliest attested graphic form of 樣 and a dated sequence of its oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical forms were not established: the targeted paleographic database page could not be opened, and no inspected primary glyph evidence was obtained.

The Shuowen account is available here through a secondary database reference; the original entry was not directly inspected. Its claim that 樣 denotes an oak fruit is a historical lexicographic assertion, not verified earliest usage.

The Tang and Song literary citations establish examples of the ‘form’ and ‘kind’ senses, but do not establish when or by what semantic steps the graph’s wood/tree-related sense developed into those abstract senses.
No independent evidence establishes a sound-based borrowing from an oak/tree name to the word meaning form or pattern; do not assert that mechanism from the shared graph alone.

The modern simplified graph replaces 羕 with 羊 in the component position, but the scheme itself only lists the character mapping; the specific editorial rationale for that component substitution is not documented by the inspected normative source.

Official Unihan character-specific pages for U+6837 and U+6A23 and the Xiaoxuetang 樣 page returned access errors. The supplied local rows give kMandarin yàng for both; these readings are metadata and not evidence of an ancient sound relationship.

No Baxter–Sagart readings for 樣, 羕, or 羊 were supplied in the local-primary input, and no verified external Baxter–Sagart row was obtained; Zhengzhang *laŋs/*laŋ is retained as a distinct reconstruction system.

No primary excavated or dated paleographic specimen of 樣 was inspected. Shuowen-style seal material is a lexicographic form, not evidence for earliest attestation; a chronological oracle-bone/bronze/seal/clerical sequence remains unestablished.

The Shuowen account preserved by the Ministry dictionary supports 木 and 羕 and an oak-fruit gloss. The bridge from the tree/fruit sense to later form, pattern, kind, sample and classifier senses remains undated and unproven. Do not infer a sequence from a modern gloss list.

The separate older graph 样 has an independently recorded yáng sense for a silkworm-tray support post and a yàng sense referring to 樣. Available inspected material does not date or fully explain the relationship between these senses and the simplified form.

Zhengzhang-style *laŋs (羕, 樣) and *laŋ (羊) are secondary reconstruction data; Baxter–Sagart local row for 羕 is *[ɢ](r)aŋʔ-s, but no verified Baxter–Sagart row for 樣 was obtained. These systems must not be merged. The traditional compound's proposed phonetic is 羕, not modern simplified 羊.
Local Unihan rows report yàng for 樣, 样 and 羕, but the two official Unicode lookups were inaccessible. The local readings are metadata, not ancient phonetic evidence.

The proposed 羕 seal image is a modern vector reconstruction from Commons, not an artifact photograph. Its original image URL was established on the inspected description page, but the direct fetch returned cache miss; downstream image acquisition and pixel review remain necessary.

The dossier's reported Tang and Song model/kind citations were not independently confirmed here because the Revised Mandarin Dictionary page returned no inspectable content. No dated attestations for these senses are claimed in this result.

No dated oracle-bone, bronze, or other excavated specimen of 樣 was inspected; the Shuowen witness and Ministry dictionary’s indexed sources establish a traditional lexicographic analysis, not an artifact-dated graphic chronology.

The Shuowen oak-fruit gloss is directly attested as a historical dictionary statement, but it is not shown to be the earliest lexical sense. The semantic bridge, if any, from oak fruit to form, kind, sample/model, pronoun, and classifier remains undated and unproven.
The Tang and Song citations provide dated occurrences of the form/shape and kind senses respectively, but do not establish first attestation or a chronology between senses.

The exact upstream Unihan lookups for 羕, 木 and 樣 returned Internal Error in this web session. Local supplied kMandarin rows report yàng for 羕 and 樣 and mù for 木; these are local metadata, not externally verified page contents or evidence of an ancient sound relationship.

No verified Baxter–Sagart entry for 樣 or 羊 was obtained. The supplied local 羕 row reads MC yangH and OC *[ɢ](r)aŋʔ-s, while local 木 reads MC muwk and OC *C.mˤok; these local rows are not external citations and cannot establish the compound’s historical sound relation by themselves.

The separate graph 样 has an older yáng sense for a wooden support used with silkworm trays according to dossier evidence, but the external page for that entry yielded no inspectable content in this pass. Its relationship to standardized simplified 样 and its chronology remain uncertain.
The specific reason the 1956 standardized simplified form uses 羊 where traditional 樣 has 羕 was not established by the inspected sources.
The current Ministry dictionary confirms classifier use in its 2021 entry, but does not establish the first historical occurrence or development of that use.

The selected 木 and 羕 images are modern digital drawings in Shuowen seal-script style, not artifact photographs or dated specimens; they do not establish the earliest forms or a dated graphic sequence for 樣. The 1956 simplified-form relationship and traditional phonetic analysis are supported by existing dossier evidence, not newly re-established by these image pages.
